extracted.intended_audience: startup founders, corporate legal/IP managers, investors, and tech-industry readers
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and considerations for judging the business model, effectiveness, costs, and ethical implications of defensive patent aggregation services (e.g., RPX) that buy or license patents to indemnify members against litigation. Useful for companies deciding whether to subscribe or for analysts comparing defensive vs offensive patent funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defensive patent aggregator business model
rubrics_metrics.description: RPX markets itself as a “defensive patent aggregator.” It buys up its own patents, or strikes licensing deals on behalf of its members, and charges companies $35,000 to $4.9 million a year for perpetual licenses to those patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion captures whether the service actually aggregates patents and offers perpetual licenses to members so those patents cannot be used in litigation against members. Note the practical implication: "pay up now and any patents in RPX’s portfolio can’t be used in litigation against your company." Also relevant is the company’s explicit promise never to use its patents in litigation against companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pricing and rate-card stability
rubrics_metrics.description: "Our pricing is set on a rate card based on the value of the service, which is based on the size of your company. We are guaranteeing the rate card won’t change, other than CPI adjustments."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate cost levels (example amounts reported: $35,000 to $4.9M/year, rate card up to $5M) versus company size and budget. Consider the guarantee of rate-card stability and whether CPI-only adjustments are acceptable. Compare subscription cost to potential litigation defense costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and limits of protection
rubrics_metrics.description: RPX will only protect members from lawsuits related to its patents; "just because RPX won’t sue over the patents does not mean that the original owner won’t." Also: "It is not a vaccine, it is not perfect."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess what patents are covered (owned vs licensed), whether indemnities are broad, and whether protection covers third-party assertion by original owners. Recognize that protection is limited to RPX-controlled rights and is therefore potentially incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defensive versus offensive strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Contrast with offensive patent funds: "Nathan’s model is to make money licensing patents. We are not a fund, we don’t have capital we need to return and then generate a profit on top of that... In an offensive model, you have to build the portfolio before you can get anyone to pay you. Our pricing is set on a rate card..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the aggregator operates defensively (buying/indemnifying to prevent suits against members) or offensively (building portfolios to license or sue). Consider incentives: offensive funds may price differently and pursue litigation to monetize patents, while defensive models claim to avoid suing but may still extract protection fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-benefit relative to litigation defense
rubrics_metrics.description: Even the $35,000 a year RPX charges startups is less than defending against one patent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare subscription/licensing fees to estimated costs of defending patent litigation (legal fees, settlements, distraction). Use this as a practical metric for whether paying for membership is economically rational for a given company size and risk profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portfolio acquisition and selection strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: "We are not just looking at the technology covered by the patent, but just as important is who owns them today. If they are sitting in someone’s attic we don’t need to wake the sleeping dragon. We will buy things on the open market where we think they will end up in the hands of someone who will assert them."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how the aggregator selects patents to buy or license: focus on patents likely to be asserted, avoid acquiring patents unlikely to ever be asserted. This affects the service's defensive value and cost-efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical/framing concern: protection racket characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: “Ultimately, its business still boils down to a protection racket. An enlightened one, perhaps, but still a protection racket."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider ethical and reputational implications of paying recurring fees to avoid claims—whether the service is defensive insurance or functionally similar to extortion. This may influence corporate policy and public perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team expertise and insider knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: “What RPX really offers is a team who knows how the patent game is played, buying up patent rights on behalf of its members. They know how it is played, incidentally, because they used to play for the other side."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the team’s prior experience with patent assertion and acquisitions; insider knowledge can improve selection and defense strategies but may raise conflict-of-interest questions. Competence here is a quality metric for the service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market context and NPE litigation trends
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent trolls (NPEs) are making up an increasing percentage of all patent litigation—nearly 17 percent last year, up from about 3 percent at the beginning of the decade. Intellectual-property litigation also rises during economic downturns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use market trends (rising NPE activity, cyclical litigation increases) to judge the likely demand and value of defensive aggregation services. Higher NPE activity increases potential benefit of subscribing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness uncertainty ('hit-or-miss')
rubrics_metrics.description: "It is like mosquitoes. How do you know the one that you swatted would have stung me? It is not a vaccine, it is not perfect."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for probabilistic protection: even with a defensive portfolio, members may still be vulnerable to other patents or future assertions. Treat coverage as risk-reduction rather than full elimination of patent risk.
